newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS BEAT DEPLETED FRENCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS BEAT DEPLETED FRENCH.

text.p: South Africa beat an understrength French side 22-12 in the first of two rugby union tests on Saturday.
France, who lost six of their first-choice players in the build-up to the match, were always second best against the World Cup holders who played impressive, powerful rugby.
Tries by James Small and Andre Joubert and three penalties by flyhalf Henry Honiball gave the Springboks a useful 19-6 lead at halftime.
The French, who had managed only two penalties by winger Richard Dourthe, gave their all in the second half but failed to breach a tight South African defence.
They had to be content with two further penalties by Dourthe while Honiball landed his fourth penalty for the Springboks.
The Bordeaux clash was the first between the two sides since South Africa won 19-15 in their World Cup semifinal in Durban last year.
